![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226477/assets/d3d381842539a44e53d77697b18f0cb51552996c885a41e6681d56cba5025428.png)

The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Find  ${lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x).$
question.worked_solution:
On the left side of the graph, we see that as the values of $x$ decrease and approach $-\infty $, the graph of the function moves closer and closer to the horizontal asymptote $y=0.$ 

Consequently, $f(x)$ approaches the value $0$ as $x$ approaches $-\infty ,$ and we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x)=0.
$$

On the right side of the graph, as the values of $x$ increase and approach $\infty ,$ the graph of the function grows without bound to $\infty $ as well. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x)=\infty .
$$
